gap: No result ChatGPT got works out how much outage power the sun alone delivers for each dollar or rated kW. Enphase Sunlight Backup supports 0.30 W of load per rated AC watt, which is 71 W per IQ8 or about 17 micros to start a 1,200 W fridge. That compares with $159/kW of rated output for the battery-free Sun Gold Power SPH6548P and $333/kW for the EG4 18kPV, whose manual has a 'No Battery' outage setting it warns 'is not stable'.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Enphase pages (iq8-grid and the sunlight-backup-installation-guidelines PDF), the cited device.report Sol-Ark guides, and the top uncited result, outagemath.com. Enphase's own guide and outagemath already give the 30% rule and the 5.7 kW to 1.7 kW example. Outagemath also says EG4's batteryless output is 'not published' and that Sol-Ark needs a battery for any backup. None of these pages turns the 30% rule into watts per micro or micros per fridge start. None compares cost per rated kW across the batteryless options. None notes that the 18kPV manual itself documents a 'No Battery' outage setting with an instability warning. None mentions the battery-free Sun Gold Power SPH6548P that Dealectric lists, at $1,035.
decides: This confirms that a grid-tie-only inverter, or a Sol-Ark, gives nothing in an outage without a battery. It also splits the remaining picks by use. Enphase is the automatic, code-friendly route, but each micro supports only about 71 W of load, so it suits small essential circuits. The EG4 18kPV and Sun Gold Power SPH6548P can, on paper, carry up to their full 12 kW or 6.5 kW rating from PV with no battery. EG4 warns this output is unstable. The SPH6548P is the cheapest per rated kW at $159, but its maker page lists it as UL 1741 'for Off Grid Solar System', so it is an off-grid unit with a battery-free option, not a grid-export inverter.

findings.label: Backup load limit as share of IQ8 AC rating
findings.value: 30% (5.7 kW AC from 24 IQ8s → 1.7 kW of loads)
findings.source_title: Enphase Sunlight Backup user guide – Essential load selection
findings.note: Enphase quote: 'backup loads do not exceed 30% of the total rated AC output power of the IQ8 Microinverters'. Up to 4× 240 V or 8× 120 V circuits. Whole-home backup is 'not supported by Enphase'. Restart takes up to 2 minutes, then loads come back 22 s apart.

findings.source_title: Enphase Sunlight Backup user guide – Essential load selection

findings.label: IQ8 count needed to start a 1,200 W fridge surge (derived)
findings.value: 4.0 kW AC, which is 17 IQ8s at Enphase's 237.5 W per micro
findings.source_title: Solar Without a Battery in a Power Outage: What Works (OutageMath)
findings.note: OutageMath puts a fridge at about 150 W running and about 1,200 W starting. 1,200 W ÷ 0.30 = 4,000 W AC. Enphase's example gives 5,700 W ÷ 24 = 237.5 W per micro, and 4,000 ÷ 237.5 = 16.8, rounded up to 17.

findings.label: Add-on cost per kW of backup load, 24-micro example (derived)
findings.source_title: Solar Without a Battery in a Power Outage: What Works (OutageMath)
findings.note: OutageMath estimates the IQ System Controller 3 plus load controllers at $3,000–3,500 in parts, before labor and not counting the micros. $3,000 ÷ 1.71 kW = $1,754 and $3,500 ÷ 1.71 kW = $2,047. This is OutageMath's estimate, not an Enphase price.

findings.label: Batteryless outage operation
findings.value: Supported by a 'No Battery' setting, with a 'not stable' warning
findings.note: p.84: "'No Battery' can be enabled to use solar power to supply load when the grid fails or load-shedding happens." p.50: "in this situation the Off-Grid energy is supplied by solar and is not stable." No batteryless output derate is published.

findings.label: Price and cost per rated AC kW (derived)
findings.note: List price $4,898.00. Rated output 12,000 W, so $3,999.99 ÷ 12 kW = $333/kW. The EG4 maker page shows no price and lists 18 kW PV input. Signature Solar lists 21,000 W 'recommended PV input'.
